governanceNotes: Bidirectionality is the controlling guard: the same sources that quantify comorbidity describe anxiety as a predisposing factor for chronic dizziness, so neither direction is asserted; the anxiety-disorder source-identity direction (anxiety producing psychogenic dizziness) would belong on that file's edge set if authored separately.
Referred-population ascertainment: 79.3% and 88% figures come from tertiary neuro-otology cohorts enriched for chronic functional dizziness; general-dizziness populations show lower rates.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Tertiary neuro-otology cohort of 1,552 consecutive vertigo patients: chronic subjective dizziness diagnosed in 164 patients (10.6%), with psychiatric disorder - mainly anxiety - found in 79.3% of cases and anxiety described as a strong predisposing factor (Odman & Maire 2008); Barany-criteria PPPD cohort (n=75): psychiatric comorbidity present in 88%, most commonly combined anxiety and depression (Kothari 2026); neuro-otology review: psychiatric comorbidity rates near 50% in structural vestibular syndromes with the highest rates in vestibular migraine and Meniere's disease, and anxiety-related postural-strategy change as a proposed mechanism (Dieterich & Staab 2017).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the comorbidity is quantified in referred tertiary populations with ascertainment bias; anxiety is documented as a predisposing factor for chronic dizziness, demonstrating bidirectionality (anxiety can precede and follow vestibular symptoms); the PPPD construct itself involves anxiety as the bridge between acute vestibular events and chronic dizziness; shared vestibular-limbic pathways are hypothesized, not validated as one-direction causation.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized maladaptive postural-control pathway: a vestibular insult or chronic dizziness state triggers heightened vigilance to motion and postural threat; anxiety-related changes in postural strategy (high-frequency corrective movements, leg-muscle co-contraction, visual dependence) and altered cortical integration of vestibular, visual, and proprioceptive signals produce persistent non-spinning dizziness with avoidance behavior; recurrent attacks consolidate anticipatory anxiety meeting anxiety-disorder criteria. Shared vestibular-limbic connectivity makes the loop bidirectional, so chronic dizziness can precipitate an anxiety disorder while pre-existing anxiety amplifies dizziness chronification.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: GAD-7 or structured-clinical-interview diagnosis of an anxiety disorder in a patient with documented vestibular disorder or chronic dizziness; temporal documentation distinguishing antecedent anxiety from anxiety developing after vestibular onset; exclusion of medication-induced dizziness and vestibular-migraine interictal states
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented vestibular diagnosis or chronic-dizziness syndrome as the antecedent condition; anxiety-disorder diagnosis by GAD-7 threshold or structured interview; clinical chronology distinguishing anxiety developing after vestibular onset from pre-existing anxiety disorder
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pre-existing anxiety disorder predisposing to chronic dizziness (reverse direction)
Medication-induced dizziness including SSRIs and vestibular suppressants

evidenceGaps: Documented vestibular diagnosis or chronic-dizziness syndrome (PPPD criteria, chronic subjective dizziness) as the antecedent condition
Anxiety-disorder diagnosis by GAD-7 threshold or structured interview rather than transient situational anxiety
Clinical chronology distinguishing anxiety developing after vestibular onset from pre-existing anxiety disorder
Exclusion of vestibular suppressant medication effects and vestibular-migraine phenotypes as alternative explanations for both symptoms
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: comorbidity is quantified (79.3% of chronic subjective dizziness; 88% of PPPD) but in tertiary-referred populations with documented bidirectionality - anxiety predisposes to chronic dizziness and chronic dizziness precipitates anxiety - precluding one-direction attribution.

sourceReferences.citation: Odman M, Maire R. Chronic subjective dizziness. Acta Otolaryngol. 2008;128(10):1085-8. PMID 18607990.
sourceReferences.note: Retrospective cohort (n=1,552 vertigo referrals): CSD in 164 patients (10.6%); psychiatric disorder, mainly anxiety, found in 79.3% of CSD cases; anxiety a strong predisposing factor; balance and emotion share common neurologic pathways allowing reciprocal provocation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 18607990; anxiety in 79.3% of chronic subjective dizziness

sourceReferences.citation: Dieterich M, Staab JP. Functional dizziness: from phobic postural vertigo and chronic subjective dizziness to persistent postural-perceptual dizziness. Curr Opin Neurol. 2017;30(1):107-113. PMID 28002123.
sourceReferences.note: Review: functional dizziness is the primary cause in ~10% of neuro-otology presentations; psychiatric comorbidity near 50% in structural vestibular syndromes, highest with vestibular migraine and Meniere's; precipitating events trigger anxiety-related postural-strategy changes with increased motion vigilance and muscle co-contraction.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 28002123; anxiety-related postural mechanism and comorbidity rates
